artifact_revision: agentmux a3c3cfbb + the session-18 working tree as it was measured, uncommitted. amx 0.8.0 built from that tree by `go build` (what `just build` runs; revision a3c3cfbb7fd1-dirty, sha256:efd425550366) and laid out as a bundle; what was edited after the recorded runs changes no behaviour of amx: two package comments, the documentation, one lifecycle test helper and the example-config shape test. tmux 3.7c packaged runtime: the signed one from the session-17 Release bundle (macos/build/Agent Mux.app/Contents/Resources/tmux, bin/tmux sha256 fb421000337b…, SHA256SUMS 858d25c2c2d4f810…) for the real-daemon run, and the same build before signing (macos/Vendor/tmux/bin/tmux, sha256 51f8bc96377b…) for the in-process budgets. Agent Mux.app Debug test host built on the MacBook Pro from the synced tree for the hosted suite; no Swift source changed in this session.
method: Three recorded runs. (1) session-18/fleet-budgets.log and fleet-budgets.json: `AMX_PERF_TESTS=1 go test -run TestPerformance_ ./internal/daemon` with AMX_TMUX set to the packaged tmux, on the Studio (Apple M2 Ultra, 24 cores, macOS 27.0.1): for 1, 10 and 30 stand-in agents, idle (`sleep`) and under sustained output (`yes`: every pane printing as fast as the server takes it), a real private tmux server with the production configuration and the daemon's own maintenance pass and screen-read path, 30 passes and 10 sweeps each. (2) session-18/production-fleet.log (78 checks, 0 failed) and the files beside it: session-18/driver/run.sh starts the real `amx daemon start` and the packaged tmux in a world of its own on the Studio (HOME and TMPDIR under /tmp/amxs18, system-only PATH under `env -i`, notifications and ASL off, no Kitty), launches the same six fleets with `amx project launch --backend tmux`, and reads the daemon's and the server's CPU time and memory from `ps` over a 30 s window each; then, with 30 agents printing, takes doctor, debug status and a share bundle, greps everything for planted canaries, and breaks the backend three ways. Headless: nothing was shown and no input was sent on the Studio; the operator's daemon, tmux, Kitty and AgentMux state were not read or written, and the world was removed at exit (verified). (3) session-18/mac-test-remote.log: `just mac-test` through the remote route, the hosted suite on Seb's MacBook Pro (377 tests, 0 failures), for the app-side rendering bound. Unit and contention tests are in session-18/go-test.log. Contention: session-18/stress-concurrent.log is the concurrent phase of `just reliability-stress` run alone (the whole suite as load, 82 packages ok, with four shards of the stress scenarios x20 racing it, all four ok), which includes the new `TestHandler_ConcurrentHealthDuringRuntimeMaintenance`. One complete `just reliability-stress` was run before that and failed in this phase on `TestServer_GoroutinesDrainAfterShutdownRequest` (a state update not acknowledged within the 250 ms hook budget under load); the same failure reproduced on the unmodified a3c3cfbb checkout, the test was repaired to wait on the liveness grace like the other lifecycle scenarios, and the phase then passed twice (the second run is the log). The isolated and `-race` repetitions passed in that first run; the complete recipe was not run again here.
limits: One machine and one run of each measurement; `ps` reports CPU time in hundredths of a second, so the daemon's share is known to about 0.03% of a core over 30 s. The agents are stand-ins, not harnesses: `yes` is an upper bound on output no agent reaches, and an idle `sleep` prints nothing at all. The real daemon reads no tmux pane today (its screen probes read Kitty windows), so `screen captures` was `no screen read yet` throughout the real-daemon run and no daemon capture freshness was observed live; what a read of a tmux pane costs is measured in-process only. No terminal was attached in the real-daemon run (attached = 0 of 30); the attached count is exercised by the in-process test with a real pseudo-terminal viewer. The world had no Kitty, so a mixed Kitty and tmux daemon was not measured, and the daemon was `degraded` for its whole life there (warning `daemon_degraded`: no initial Kitty snapshot). The app was not part of the fleet run: 30 embedded Ghostty surfaces were not measured, and the rendering bound is the hosted test of the occlusion rule, not a GPU or energy measurement. The overview's four-read capture ceiling was exercised by its unit tests (tui/overview in go-test.log), not by a live overview over 30 tmux panes. The amx measured is a local build of the working tree, not the binary inside a signed bundle; the bundle was not rebuilt in this session.

backend-failure-diagnosis.evidence: Observed in session-18/production-fleet.log (three `backend failure` cases, 12 checks, 0 failed). (1) The tmux server holding 30 agents was stopped with SIGSTOP: 40 s later `amx doctor --strict` exited 2 and printed `backend: … server running but not answering` with failure `backend_server_unreadable`, warning `runtime_reconcile_failing` (`the last 4 reconciliation passes failed (timeout)`) and note `tmux_client_timeouts` (session-18/doctor-server-stopped.txt; `failure_class: timeout`, `consecutive_failures: 4` in the JSON); the registry still held all 30 agents live and the daemon still answered. After SIGCONT `amx doctor --strict` exited 0 with `runtime sessions: 30 live` (session-18/doctor-server-recovered.txt), and the journal held exactly one `reconcile_failed` record (class timeout, 6002.4 ms, 30 live sessions) and one `reconcile_recovered` for the whole outage (session-18/journal-runtime-reconcile.json). (2) The server was killed with SIGKILL: every agent was recorded as stopped and none relaunched, doctor printed `no server running` and `runtime sessions: 0 live` (session-18/doctor-server-killed.txt), and the journal recorded the pass that found 30 agents gone, naming them by runtime-session ID only (session-18/journal-runtime-reconcile-killed.json). (3) A standalone amx with no bundle, no tmux on PATH and no daemon: `amx doctor --strict` exited 2 with `daemon: unreachable`, `backend: launches go to tmux; no usable tmux; no server running`, `versions: … tmux not found (needs 3.5 or newer)` and failure `backend_tmux_unavailable` with each place tried and `brew install tmux` (session-18/doctor-no-tmux.txt). None of these outputs contained a canary.
